sections.content: How many people are "tyre, exhaust and windscreen fitters"?

13,270 people

were counted on the census as "tyre, exhaust and windscreen fitters" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Tyre, exhaust and windscreen fitters fit, repair and adjust tyres, exhausts and windscreens on cars, buses, motorcycles and other motor vehicles.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "tyre, exhaust and windscreen fitters" there were more men than women (97.5% compared with 2.5%).

This means "tyre, exhaust and windscreen fitters" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "process, plant and machine operatives".

Men made up 97.4% and women made up 2.6% of "tyre, exhaust and windscreen fitters"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "tyre, exhaust and windscreen fitters" included:

  • groundsmen and greenkeepers
  • sheet metal workers
  • vehicle paint technicians

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years. Of the whole working population 7.9% were aged 20 to 24 years. For people working as "tyre, exhaust and windscreen fitters", 14.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "tyre, exhaust and windscreen fitters" was 65 years or older.

We can look at who worked as "tyre, exhaust and windscreen fitters" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

The percentage of men and women who are "tyre, exhaust and windscreen fitters" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "tyre, exhaust and windscreen fitters", 7.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (84.6% compared with 15.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (86.6%) than self-employed (13.4%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
